auth: OAuth2 client-credentials grant for a Jamf Pro API Client: POST {base_url}/v1/oauth/token with form-encoded client_id/client_secret (grant_type=client_credentials) returns a bearer access_token (short-lived, ~30 min default TTL; re-request when expired). Alternative: POST {base_url}/v1/auth/token with HTTP Basic credentials of a Jamf Pro API-role account; refresh via POST /v1/auth/refresh-token and revoke via POST /v1/auth/invalidate-token. The same bearer token is honored by classic /JSSResource endpoints (which live at the instance root, outside /api). Provision a least-privilege API role with only Read privileges for the endpoints below (Read Computers, Read Mobile Devices, Read Smart Computer Groups, Read Static Computer Groups, Read Policies, Read User-Initiated Enrollment, View Local Admin Password Audit History, Read Device Compliance Information); write commands (POST /v2/mdm/commands) are approval-gated per playbook decision D7 and are never issued autonomously.

endpoints.purpose: OAuth2 client-credentials exchange: client_id + client_secret -> bearer access_token for an API Client (least-privilege, secret-rotatable).

Basic-auth token exchange: HTTP Basic (API-role username/password) -> bearer JWT; supported alternative for tenants not using API Clients (Jamf recommends API Clients as more secure and has not deprecated this path).
Refresh an unexpired bearer token issued via /v1/auth/token.
Revoke the current bearer token on integration teardown/rotation.

Paginated macOS computer inventory (totalCount/results envelope; page, page-size, sort, RSQL filter params). section=GENERAL,HARDWARE,APPLICATIONS,SECURITY,PURCHASING,... trims the payload to the sections a control needs.
Single computer inventory record for drill-down on one device.
Full detail record: applications, localUserAccounts, certificates, configurationProfiles and groupMemberships (groupId/groupName/smartGroup) for one computer.
Paginated iOS/iPadOS/tvOS device inventory with RSQL filter; the v1 equivalent is deprecated, use v2.
Full mobile device detail incl. security block (activationLockEnabled, passcodeCompliant, hardwareEncryption, jailBreakDetected) and managementId used for MDM commands.
List of configured patch titles (third-party + Apple) that Jamf tracks for version currency; classic /JSSResource/patchsoftwaretitles is deprecated in its favor.
Per-version install counts for one patch title - quantifies how many devices still run old, unpatched software versions.
Patch policies that enforce version/deadline-driven installs; pair with GET /v2/patch-policies/{id}/logs for per-device outcomes.
macOS managed software-update state (download/install/available) for one computer, evidencing OS-update delivery.

Jamf Managed Local Admin Passwords (LAPS) settings: auto-deploy and auto-rotation of the local admin password. Companion reads: /v2/local-admin-password/{clientManagementId}/accounts and /account/{username}/audit.
Audit trail of who viewed/rotated a managed local admin password - access-to-device-credentials is attributable.

Queue an MDM command (DEVICE_LOCK, ERASE_DEVICE, ENABLE_LOST_MODE, SET_RECOVERY_LOCK, RESTART_DEVICE...) against clientData[].managementId, e.g. erase with return-to-service for device recovery. WRITE action: execute only behind human approval (D7); evidence read is the command history/audit.
Per-computer device-compliance state surfaced to conditional access (privilege: Read Device Compliance Information) - devices must report healthy state to keep access.
Classic API (instance root, no /api prefix): smart computer group definition incl. criteria (name/search_type/value) - scoping used to detect unauthorized software and gate remediation.
Classic API: policy detail incl. general.enabled and self_service payloads - policies deliver Self Service content such as security-awareness training.
Classic API: smart user group definition (is_smart, criteria, users) - role-based scoping used to target specialized training and privileged device access.
